item.title: DOJ charges 28 with unlawful voting, other election-related offenses in California
item.description: The DOJ has charged 28 individuals in California with election-related offenses, and did not rule out prosecuting election workers who are "processing the ballots" there.

item.title: Parents of school shooting victim hire attorneys to probe school plans, gun purchase
item.description: The parents of one of three children killed in last week’s shooting at an elementary school in Bend, Oregon, have hired attorneys to investigate the school’s protocols and how the teenage gunman got his weapon

item.title: Ronaldo suspended for 30 days and fined for walking out on Portugal camp
item.description: Walking out on the Portugal camp has earned Cristiano Ronaldo a 30-day suspension and 255 euros fine from the national federation

item.title: WATCH: Teen on how he turned 3D printing idea into a profitable business
item.description: Just three months after graduating high school, Mike Satterlee began using his 3D printer to make hard-shell insulated drink koozies he calls "can coolers."

item.title: Spain floods kill four as torrential rain inundates eastern regions
item.description: Torrential rain battered eastern Spain on Monday, killing at least four people in recent days as floodwaters swept away cars, submerged roads and stranded residents. Emergency crews carried out more than 400 rescues in Valencia, where rainfall reached 700 litres per square metre in 24 hours in some areas.

item.title: France tells online marketplaces to crack down on resale of looted items
item.description: As thousands of shop owners are reeling from the weekend violence and looting, listings of apparently stolen items have been popping up online. The government asked major second-hand marketplaces such as Vinted, eBay and Amazon to crack down on suspicious adverts.

item.title: Supreme Court to hear case on race in middle school admissions
item.description: The Supreme Court has agreed to hear a case about race in middle school admissions

item.title: Le Pen 'trying to use these events to push her popularity', expert says
item.description: In the wake of the weekend's violence, the political camps have been trading blame for the “chaos”. The riots have played into the hands of the far-right National Rally - which has been quick to capitalise on the anger and fears over law and order. Speaking with FRANCE 24's Mark Owen, Dr David Lees, Reader in French Studies at the University of Warwick, says that Marine Le Pen "is trying to use these events as a vehicle for pushing her popularity ahead of the elections next year".

item.title: Mahmoud Khalil appeals to Supreme Court to sue Trump admin over free speech
item.description: Pro-Palestinian activist Mahmoud Khalil appeals to the U.S. Supreme Court, seeking to sue the government for allegedly violating his First Amendment rights.

item.title: Shawn Oliver pleads not guilty to OUI charge after crash
item.description: Shawn Oliver has pleaded not guilty to charges of operating under the influence and other related offenses after suspending his campaign for lieutenant governor of Massachusetts

item.title: Art crime detective Arthur Brand warns: 'All museums have been, and will be, victims of theft'
item.description: François Picard is pleased to welcome art crime detective Arthur Brand. "In the old days they stole a painting, but a painting is unique; you cannot cut it in two," explains Brand, "In the last 10 years they have been targeting more and more objects made of gold, silver". He examines the transformation of international art theft, warning that increasingly sophisticated criminal opportunism is shifting attention from irreplaceable paintings towards precious metals and gemstones that can be dismantled, melted down or dispersed.

item.title: LIVE: ABC News Live
item.description: 24/7 coverage of breaking news and live events

item.title: France riots: AI photos falsely depict elderly couple ‘stripped and robbed’
item.description: AI-generated photos falsely claiming to show an elderly couple being “stripped and robbed” during unrest in France have racked up millions of views. Amplified by far-right accounts, the images fuelled inflammatory claims about Muslims, Jews and the riots. The FRANCE 24 Observers traced one image to an AI photo montage published by a pro-Israel account. The images were created using OpenAI tools, and the alleged assault remains unverified, with no official reports confirming the attack.

item.title: Japan launches mission to Mars to bring back samples from its moon
item.description: Japan launched a spacecraft towards Mars in a ground-breaking mission to bring back samples from the largest of the planet's two moons.

item.title: France faces reckoning with public order policing after violent protest weekend
item.description: France reeled Monday after a weekend of nationwide unrest sparked by mass protests against the rising cost of living and in support of high school students’ demands over education funding. In the violent clashes that erupted, law enforcement officers and protesters were wounded, public buildings were set ablaze and businesses were looted, raising significant questions about the French police's approach to public order.

item.title: French far right seeks to capitalise on protests with calls for law and order
item.description: In the wake of the weekend's violence, the political camps have been trading blame for the “chaos”. The riots have played into the hands of the far-right National Rally, which has been quick to capitalise on the anger and fears over law and order. FRANCE 24's Emerald Maxwell takes a look.

item.title: Russia-China-US summit would prolong the war, Kyiv says
item.description: Ukrainian ⁠Foreign Minister ​Andrii Sybiha said on ​Monday that a summit between Russia, China ​and the ‌US would ⁠encourage President Vladimir Putin ‌to prolong the war. The ​Wall Street Journal reported that Putin had proposed a ​summit next month ​with US ​President Donald Trump and Chinese President ​Xi Jinping to negotiate an end to the war on terms ⁠that would favour Moscow. FRANCE 24's Monte Francis reports.

item.title: Iran live updates: Russia says it won't stop cooperating with Iran
item.description: Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov said Russia does not intend to abandon its agreements with Iran in the economic and investment spheres.

item.title: Paris weekend riots raise concerns for tourism industry
item.description: France announced partial curfews in Paris and other cities on Monday after weekend demonstrations over soaring prices degenerated into some of the worst street violence in recent years. Images of riots and looting in France over the weekend have been seen across the world and are worrying the country's tourism industry. Could the violence put off foreign tourists from visiting? FRANCE 24's Selina Sykes reports.

item.title: Zelensky says Starshield speed limits slowing down frontline response
item.description: Speed limits on a US military grade satellite system are hindering Ukrainian forces' ability to coordinate drone strikes against Russian forces, President Volodymyr Zelensky said on Monday. Zelensky said frontline units had reported that the Starshield equipment "stops functioning at speeds of 130-160 kilometres (80-100 miles) per hour in various sectors of the front". Separately, a Ukrainian army brigade has announced the rescue of a wounded soldier from the front line using an aerial drone, describing the evacuation as the first of its kind. The brigade published a video showing the drone lowering itself to the ground, before a man in combat gear fastens himself to a winch onboard and is lifted upwards. FRANCE 24's Gulliver Cragg reports from Ukraine.

item.title: Ex-OpenAI worker accused of bugging offices planned to 'flee' to Saudi Arabia, prosecutors say
item.description: A former OpenAI engineer charged with secretly installing a recording device at its offices was "mere days" away from fleeing to Saudi Arabia before his arrest, prosecutors allege.

item.title: WATCH: Is using cash for purchases becoming a thing of the past?
item.description: Lawmakers on Capitol Hill are considering bills to keep cash an option in commerce.

item.title: France: ‘localised’ curfews announced after weekend of violence
item.description: Following a weekend of #violence and #looting, the French government has announced localised #curfews, financial support for affected businesses and a tougher judicial response, while keeping the option of a state of emergency on the table.

item.title: DZ Mafia murder trial set to begin near Marseille
item.description: Five men with alleged connections to the major criminal group DZ Mafia are accused of murdering, in 2020, the elder brother of anti-drug activist Amine Kessaci – now deputy mayor of Aix-en-Provence. The trial, set to begin on Monday, highlights the threat posed by mafia-style drug trafficking networks in the region. FRANCE 24’s Delano D’Souza reports.

item.title: Ukraine deploys drone to airlift wounded soldier in 'world-first' operation
item.description: Ukraine has evacuated a wounded soldier from the front line using an aerial drone in what a Ukrainian army brigade has described as a world-first operation. The successful mission highlights the growing role of unmanned technology in battlefield evacuations as drones continue to shape the conflict between Ukraine and Russia.

item.title: France wants curfews in some areas after weekend of riots
item.description: France's central government asked some local authorities to impose curfews and faced pressure over security failings on Monday after a weekend of riots and looting borne out of nationwide anti-government protests. Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu did not rule out declaring state of emergency but said it was more appropriate for now to apply partial and localised curfews, without providing details of which cities would be affected.

item.title: France protests: Who are the people arrested during the unrest?
item.description: At least 2,400 people were arrested in France during protests over the weekend, some simply for being in the wrong place at the wrong time, others on suspicion of theft and looting. In an official address, French President Emmanuel Macron warned that “those who looted will have to pay for the damage”. But who exactly are these rioters?

item.title: 'Police weren't overwhelmed by people protesting and marching' about education and cost of living
item.description: Oliver Farry is pleased to welcome Andrew Smith, Lecturer in Liberal Arts at Queen Mary University of London. France's escalating social unrest has exposed a troubling disconnect between legitimate popular grievances and the government's increasingly security-focused response. Smith argues that the violence accompanying otherwise largely peaceful demonstrations reveals serious failures of policing, while President Emmanuel Macron's response offers "very little of substance." Drawing parallels with France's historic protest movements, Smith identifies a "convergence of causes" rooted in economic insecurity, educational inequalities and political paralysis. He warns that a repressive response risks deepening the crisis, calling instead for a renewed commitment to "participatory social democracy."

item.title: King Charles 'sends books about soil' to Aung San Suu Kyi
item.description: Myanmar's detained former leader Aung San Suu Kyi has been photographed receiving books and letters from the King Charles, officials said.

item.title: Object thought to be Amelia Earhart’s missing plane likely just 'large trees', researchers find
item.description: An expedition to investigate if an anomaly seen on a satellite image of a remote island in the South Pacific was Amelia Earhart’s missing plane has ended without recovering the wreckage.

item.title: Four soldiers dead, dozens injured in fire at Canada military base
item.description: Four soldiers were killed and dozens injured in a fire at a military base in Alberta province, one of the worst peacetime tragedies to hit Canada's armed forces on home soil, Prime Minister Mark Carney said Sunday.

item.title: French PM says 'ultra-left' seeking 'deep unrest' ahead of election
item.description: French Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu on Monday accused the "ultra-left movement" of seeking to "orchestrate deep unrest across the country" in the runup to next year's presidential election. FRANCE 24 International Affairs Editor Angela Diffley looks back at Lecornu's remarks in the wake of the violent protests that shook the country over the weekend.

item.title: Brazil court orders Meta to prove it gives Lula, Bolsonaro campaign content equal treatment
item.description: Brazil’s top electoral court has given Meta 24 hours to prove it is treating campaign content from incumbent President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva and Senator Flavio Bolsonaro equally on its online platforms, threatening a daily fine for noncompliance. The ruling follows allegations from Lula's campaign that the social media giant is suppressing Lula’s campaign content ahead of Sunday’s closely contested presidential runoff.

item.title: UEFA writes to FIFA demanding answers on Trump-Infantino dealings
item.description: European football chiefs have sent a list of 42 questions to FIFA, demanding answers about Gianni Infantino's alleged "conflicts of interest" over business dealings with the Trump family and the World Cup sell-off attempt.

item.title: France protests draw global attention: Trump, Vance blame immigration for unrest
item.description: US President Donald Trump on Sunday blamed immigration for unrest during protests in France and urged the country to tighten its migration rules. Trump's post comes after similar comments made by Vice President JD Vance on Saturday. Vance, who is seen as a potential presidential candidate in the 2028 election, also drew a connection to upcoming midterm races for congressional seats on November 3, where Republicans are not expected to perform well. FRANCE 24's Fraser Jackson reports from the United States.

item.title: Macron kicks off three-day Gulf tour, seeks securing fuel supplies amid crisis
item.description: French President Emmanuel Macron on Monday began a Gulf tour aimed at securing oil and diesel supplies in an effort to bring down prices, after a weekend of violent protests sparked by soaring living costs. Macron, just hours after slamming France's "unbridled" violence in an address late on Sunday, arrived in OPEC member Kuwait where he was welcomed by the emir, Sheikh Mishal Al-Ahmad Al-Jaber Al-Sabah. FRANCE 24's International Affairs Editor Kethevane Gorjestani tells us more.

item.title: Drone attacks kill scores in Sudan's West Kordofan state and capital Khartoum
item.description: At least 80 people were killed in a drone strike near a market in Sudan’s southern West Kordofan state, a medical source and a witness said Monday, in one of the deadliest single attacks since the Sudan war erupted in 2023. A separate drone attack Monday in the capital Khartoum killed four, including three children.

item.title: Bipartisan group of senators want answers on Starlink disruptions in Ukraine
item.description: The lawmakers say American personnel were endangered in attacks on Ukraine.

item.title: UN cuts food aid to half a million Gazans over funding shortages
item.description: The UN World Food Programme (WFP) has said it is being forced to "drastically reduce" aid to Gaza because of funding shortages.

item.title: Australian prime minister says lawmaker critically injured by car is 'no accident'
item.description: A car hit an Australian federal independent lawmaker on Monday, critically injuring her in an apparent deliberate attack, Prime Minister Anthony Albanese said. The driver was arrested.

item.title: Four Canadian soldiers killed after grass fire spread 'a kilometre in 36 seconds'
item.description: The four Canadian soldiers who died during a training exercise at the weekend did so when a grass fire spread "a kilometre in 36 seconds", officials said.

item.description: Doomsday cult leader Paul Mackenzie, his wife Rhoda Maweu, and 29 other co-accused have been found guilty of the murder of 190 children and one adult.

item.description: Hint: It's not only because California counts slowly.

item.description: Ten suspects have been arrested in connection with recent violence in the West Bank including attacks on an ​American ⁠photojournalist and European ⁠diplomats, Israeli police have said.

item.description: On "This Week," Energy Secretary Chris Wright defended the president's decision to waive new sanctions and tariffs meant to pressure President Vladimir Putin.

item.description: David Muir reports on the new world record for heaviest pumpkin, which weighs 3,156 pounds – smashing the previous record of 2,856 pounds set merely a week ago.

item.description: Police say the man was fishing along the shoreline at a park when he was attacked and killed by an alligator.
